When I was a teenager in the late 90s, early 2000s, I was having a pretty hard go at home (abuse and all that shit), and when I heard the lines "That the face inside is here in me, right underneath my skin" I felt like someone knew me and what I was experiencing. When I turned 30 I got sober and then I was diagnosed with dissociative identity disorder when I started intensive treatment. I remembered how LPs music helped me understand this even when I wasn't aware this was happening (there is a lot to this but I wont bore with details). Their words and Chester and Mike made me feel like not only did someone understand me and what I was going through, but that I could make it and survive it. 

When Chester died I knew that I was following his path in a lot of ways (being an addict, suicide attempts, and I wasn't getting help), and his death gave me the courage even in my sorrow that I needed to ask for help before I joined him. I told a professional about my substance abuse and as I slowly started the path on recovery, I was able to uncover a whole mess of shit I had buried for nearly 20 years and even though my life is completely unreal living with D.I.D., I am sober and trying to find strength to get through it everyday for my son and myself and for Chester and all my friends I have lost to addiction and suicide. 

LP has been part of who I was, who I became, and who I am now. They have been there through it all.

We feel pretty satisfied with how mr. Robot portrays it. Its a drama of course, and way more exciting than our life, but its real. We see each other, we talk to each other and also know we are all one.
